Twin of the Kotlin `val OuraSpO2.channel` in android/app/src/main/java/com/noop/oura/OuraEvents.kt. Both are one-line extension properties over OuraSpO2 returning OuraSpO2Channel, added together in the same change. Kotlin declares its copy as a TOP-LEVEL extension property with a dotted receiver, which the ledger's Kotlin property scan does not index, so the Swift side reads as one-sided. The pair is real; only one half is visible to the inventory.

Restores the previously shipped Android Ring 4 adapter from durable Room OURA_HRV events to explicit sleep-window hints. This is an Android fork recovery path after PR #1 omitted its integration, not a new shared scoring formula. Apple does not consume this Android persistence adapter; the shared stage and HRV computations remain unchanged.

Android fork overload restores the optional sleepWindowHints input used by the Ring 4 Room/native-resting and manual-sleep integration. An empty hint list preserves the common detector path. The extra input is Android-specific; it does not replace the shared scoring algorithms or claim an Apple implementation.

Android fork manual-sleep repair adds the default-false allowCardioOnly option for user-supplied Ring 4 bounds, whose source has no continuous gravity stream. Other callers retain the motion-density gate. This restores the Android UI-to-Room editing workflow; no corresponding Apple edit flow is changed.

Android Room suspend-query facade for the restored native-HRV comparison UI. It exposes the existing eventsByKind DAO query without a schema change or a new stored value. Apple persistence uses GRDB and does not share this Room facade.

Android BluetoothDevice addresses rotate for Oura Ring 4, so the restored scanner uses the advertised serial where available and authenticates candidate devices with locally stored keys. These Android advertisement-selection helpers do not apply to CoreBluetooth peripheral UUID identity on Apple.
